question: Your CI pipeline runs Claude Code to review each pull request. The system prompt has detailed rules for the review comment format, but the output still varies: some comments omit the file location, and others omit the severity or the suggested fix. You decide to add few-shot examples to the prompt. Which choices about the set of examples would most effectively make the review comments consistent and actionable?

options.text: Choose two to four examples that cover different kinds of genuine findings, such as a security flaw and a null-reference bug.
options.reason: The guide recommends a small targeted set of 2-4 examples, and varied examples help Claude Code generalize the format to new findings instead of matching only pre-specified cases.

options.text: Make each example a complete review comment that shows the location, issue, severity, and suggested fix in the exact desired format.
options.reason: The guide says that few-shot examples that demonstrate the specific desired output format (location, issue, severity, suggested fix) are the most effective way to get consistent output when detailed instructions alone fail.

options.text: Vary the order and layout of the fields from example to example so that Claude Code learns that several formats are acceptable.
options.reason: The guide says that examples should demonstrate one specific desired output format to achieve consistency, so examples with varied layouts teach inconsistency.

options.text: Show only the issue description in each example, and leave the location, severity, and fix to the written format rules.
options.reason: The written format rules alone already produce inconsistent comments, and the guide says the examples must demonstrate the complete desired format to achieve consistency.

options.text: Collect about twenty examples, one for each known type of defect, so that Claude Code can match each new finding to a listed case.
options.reason: The guide recommends 2-4 targeted examples, and it says that examples should enable generalization to novel patterns rather than matching only pre-specified cases.
